subject: Post-call: Long-context evals / recommended models / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Lee <jenna.lee@acme.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps: long-context evals & model recs

Hi Jenna / Tom 1

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we can prioritize the eval work your team needs: 

Summary of needs:
- Primary goal: reliable end-to-end summarization of multi-document customer support threads (avg 25–40k tokens), keeping key metadata intact (timestamps, customer IDs, action items).
- Key success metrics: compression fidelity (ROUGE/ROUGE-L), instruction-following accuracy on action-item extraction, and truncation/continuity behavior across window boundaries.
- Constraints: on-prem PII controls, eventual VPC deployment, prefer models with strong quantization support for Dedicated pools.

Recommendations from the call (short-list for initial eval):
- Redwood-Instruct-2-70B (quantized q4f16): best balance of instruction fidelity and long-context kernel support.
- LlamaX-65B-Long (open variant): strong sparse attention variants we've seen good summarization from on similar datasets; useful as a cost-control comparative baseline.
- FLAN-UL2 (instruction-tuned; 20B): cheaper baseline for sanity checks and regression detection.

Deliverables we’ll provide this week:
1) Prompt set: 30 representative long-thread prompts + expected structured outputs (attached: acme_long_context_promptset_v1.txt).
2) Baseline benchmarks: initial run across 3 models with token-level latency and truncation trace (attached: acme_long_context_benchmarks_v1.pdf).
3) Eval harness + scripts: instructions for running locally or we can run on a Dedicated slot if you prefer.

Open questions for your team (so we can tune evals):
- For metadata fidelity, what fields are absolutely required in the extraction vs. "nice-to-have"? (e.g., timestamps vs. agent sentiment).
- Any PII redaction rules we should apply prior to sending sample data? If yes, send the redaction spec and we’ll mirror it.

Next steps
- I’ll drop the prompt set and initial benchmark PDF (attached) now.
- Can we schedule a technical deep-dive with your ML infra lead next Tue (Aug 3) to review KV-cache behavior and Dedicated config?

If that all sounds right I’ll also open a HubSpot action (HS-ACME-447) for tracking and loop in our solutions engineer for the deep dive.

Thanks 1

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Attachments: acme_long_context_promptset_v1.txt (text), acme_long_context_benchmarks_v1.pdf (pdf)

Thanks Marissa 1 this is great, and thanks for the fast follow-up. A few quick answers / asks from our side:

- Required metadata: customer_id, created_at (timestamp), agent_id, action_items (list). Sentiment is nice-to-have but not mandatory.
- PII: we need email addresses redacted, but retain user IDs (hash is fine). I’ll send our redaction spec by EOD.
- Deep-dive: Aug 3 works for us at 10am PT. Please invite our ML infra lead (Tom).

Couple of clarifying questions on the model notes: 
1) For Redwood-Instruct-2-70B: can you confirm the truncation behavior we saw in the doc — does it do sliding-window KV cache with overlap or hard truncation at the left? That will affect how we stitch multi-document threads.
2) For the benchmark PDF: can you include a short section on "failure modes observed" (e.g., hallucinated timestamps, dropped agent responses) so we know what to watch for?

Tom / me will review the prompt set and get back with a prioritized subset we want evaluated first.

-Jenna

jenna.lee@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps: long-context evals & model recs

Thanks Jenna 1 answers inline and added a couple small updates to the deliverables.

1) Truncation / KV-cache behavior: Redwood-Instruct-2-70B (our hosted/dedicated variant) uses a sliding KV-cache with configurable left-context retention. By default we keep a soft window of the last ~16k tokens with overlap; for very long-doc summarization we recommend a chunking+summary-then-merge strategy (we included a sample orchestration script in the Drive link). Hard truncation can be configured but we avoid it by default because it often drops important lead context. (See failure-modes section in the attached PDF — we call out hallucinated timestamps and dropped agent lines observed at 20k+ naive truncation.)

2) Failure modes: included — hallucinated dates when source formatting is inconsistent; agent/assistant boundary bleed (when system messages not preserved); and thread stitching errors at abrupt turn boundaries. We added recommended mitigations per failure mode (prompting patterns and chunk overlap).

3) Prompt-set: the attached prompt set contains instructions for preserving metadata tokens as named fields (e.g., "<<CUSTOMER_ID>>"). If you’d like, Rachel can share a redaction-friendly version that masks email addresses while preserving positions.

Next steps:
- I’ve uploaded an eval harness + sample orchestration to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c_acme_longctx
- I’ll put a calendar hold for Aug 3 10:00 AM PT and add Rachel (our SRE lead) and our solutions engineer. If you prefer we run the first pass on a Dedicated slot and share the raw traces, we can do that — let me know.

Tom / Jenna — attaching the updated benchmark PDF (same filename) and the prompt-set. Let me know which subset you want prioritized and we’ll queue up the runs.

Best,

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
